chunk_findings.detail: The earlier test finding is still unanswered: `_judge_job` never looks for a recorded review round. chunk_findings.detail: The new terminal branch only consults a recorded round when `j.item` still resolves to an item. If the item id is missing, or `st.items.get(j.item)` is None, it falls through and returns `status: ready` with why `{job_id} is over (...)`. The same path fires for a detached review of a commit or branch (`j.item` empty) that was killed after the wrapper wrote an exit line and before any round was recorded.

chunk_findings.detail: The earlier objection still holds. This test still only flips `J.status` from running to `exited 0` and never records a review round, yet requires `exit == OK`, `ready == ["J1"]`, and `next_actions` mentioning `fix-X`. The job.started payload includes `item: fix-X`, so the new comment that “with no item in the log, over IS the round” does not describe this input. Given that job (exit line written, no round), the assertion still passes and locks “process over” rather than the contract stated in this file’s own docstring (wake only when the round is recorded; over with no round is not READY). The new unit tests do not close it: they never call `A.wait`, and the no-round case only covers `gone`, not `exited 0`.
